title: Robert Pattinson is officially the new James Bond, Amazon announces
text:
Robert Pattinson is officially the new James Bond, Amazon announces - Yahoo Search query for Search the web Search the web Skip to main 
 News Finance More Mail Search the web Advertisement Advertisement Return to homepage Robert Pattinson is officially the new James Bond, Amazon announces
 Adam White Updated Mon, 16 November 2026 at 3:19 pm UTC 4 min read Add Yahoo as a preferred source to see more of our stories on Google. Robert Pattinson is officially the new James Bond, Amazon announces Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond .
 The Batman actor, who has become one of the world's most famous stars since his breakout role in the Twilight franchise, called the role an "honour of a lifetime" and called his casting "a dream come true".
 "I couldn't be more excited about this partnership and the work ahead with this fantastic team," Pattinson added.
 The actor's casting brings to a close years of feverish speculation over who will play 007, after Daniel Craig formally announced his departure from the role in 2017. Names including Jack Lowden, Aaron Taylor-Johnson, Henry Cavill, Theo James, Idris Elba, Paul Mescal, James Norton, Callum Turner and Jacob Elordi have all circled the role in the past near-decade.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The casting caps a sensational year for Pattinson, who has starred in a run of commercially successful and critically acclaimed hits including Primetime , The Drama and Christopher Nolan's The Odyssey . He will next star in December's Dune: Part Three , which will mark the first of now two team-ups with filmmaker Denis Villeneuve, who is taking the reins of the new Bond film, too.
 Villeneuve, whose credits include Prisoners and the Dune trilogy, will direct from a script by Steven Knight , of Peaky Blinders fame.
 Robert Pattinson in character as James Bond (Jaap Buitendijk)
 It will also mark the first Bond film to be produced under the banner of Amazon MGM Studios, after the franchise's long-time stewards Barbara Broccoli and Michael G Wilson – who inherited 007 from super-producer Albert "Cubby" Broccoli – sold the series for a reported $1bn in 2025 .
 Terms of the deal include Amazon taking full creative control of the franchise, which could theoretically mean the arrival of future spin-off films and TV series – both of which Broccoli and Wilson were reluctant to explore when they had control of the brand.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement This was reportedly a bone of contention for Amazon , which bought MGM for $8.45bn in 2021 and had grown frustrated with what appeared to be stalled development on a new Bond film in the wake of Craig's departure. Attempts to further monetise the Bond IP had also been restrained by Broccoli and Wilson's creative control, as they reportedly shot down many Bond-related side-projects – under the pair's control, only one Bond-adjacent project launched following the MGM deal, a game show titled 007: Road to a Million in which contestants competed in spy-like challenges for money.
 With Broccoli and Wilson no longer involved in the franchise, the casting of Pattinson means that the first – and arguably most important – decision for the future of the series has been made.
 Pattinson undeniably has big shoes to fill. The casting of Daniel Craig – which was announced during a splashy press conference in October 2005 – helped revitalise a franchise that had weathered critical backlash and declining cultural relevance as Pierce Brosnan's tenure as 007 drew to a close in 2002. Craig's five Bond films collectively earned $3.5bn at the global box office and – arguably bar 2008's Quantum of Solace – drew consistently strong reviews from critics. They also returned Bond to the Oscar stage after more than 30 years, with the franchise winning the Best Original Song Oscar in 2013, 2016 and 2022.
 Daniel Craig in his first official portrait in character as James Bond, back in October 2005 (Getty Images)
 Craig was so important to the franchise that he earned a reported $25m for his starring role in 2021's No Time to Die , which sensationally killed off his James Bond in an emotional climax. The grief over Craig's departure from the role was also an ironic about-face from fans and the media, as he faced considerable criticism in 2005 when his casting was first announced. Craig – whose blonde locks differed him from his predecessors, among them Sean Connery and Roger Moore – was dubbed "Bland, James Bland" by corners of the British press, while disgruntled Bond fans launched a hate site to protest his hiring, called DanielCraigIsNotBond.com. It remains to be seen whether Pattinson will receive similar (if presumably reactionary) drubbing.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Pattinson's casting follows weeks of speculation over a series of October screen tests for Villeneuve, casting director Nina Gold and Amazon executives , with Callum Turner, Jack Lowden, Josh O'Connor and Nicholas Hoult all screen testing alongside Pattinson. It was speculated that Pattinson was the favourite, however, when reports emerged that he had been given special treatment over his fellow auditionees. Namely that he had been asked to sign up for three Bond films, rather than the four required of his rivals.
 Speaking to The Independent in June , retired casting director Debbie McWilliams – who previously cast Craig and his predecessors Brosnan and Timothy Dalton – said that the actor who plays 007 should have an air of mystery. "It is absolutely essential that [Bond] retains a total enigma," adding: "I don't want to see [a famous face] as Bond because we now know so much about them. We want to know as little about them personally as possible, because that's what spies are … He's licensed to kill, and we have to believe that he can do that. If you don't, then you've lost the audience."
